title: undo -J record
description: One journal entry `undo -J` reversed, newest first (an empty journal writes no record). Error records (`#/$defs/error`) are in the same stream. One record per line (NDJSON); version 1 of the Dogfish record format (doc/ndjson.md). Fields may be added in later releases.

undo_id.description: The id of the entry undone (`id` in `history -J`).

tool.description: The tool that recorded the entry.

undone.description: What the entry recorded, as `action` in `history -J`: `rm --safe` moved a file to the trash, or a file was moved or copied.

path_bytes.description: The bytes of `path`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form).

trash.description: Of trash: where the file was kept.

trash_bytes.description: The bytes of `trash`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`trash` then holds the lossy form).

source.description: Of move and copy: the source.

source_bytes.description: The bytes of `source`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`source` then holds the lossy form).

dest.description: Of move and copy: the destination.

dest_bytes.description: The bytes of `dest`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`dest` then holds the lossy form).

backup.description: What the destination held before, kept for undo.

backup_bytes.description: The bytes of `backup`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`backup` then holds the lossy form).

restored.description: The paths undo gave back what they held before the operation, in the order it did so: the trashed file, the moved file's source, a destination's earlier contents. Empty when nothing was left to restore.

restored_bytes.description: The bytes of every name in `restored`, base64, in the same order, present only when one of them is not UTF-8 (`restored` then holds the lossy forms).

removed.description: The paths the operation had made that undo took away (into the trash, or moved back): a copy, a move's destination.

removed_bytes.description: The bytes of every name in `removed`, base64, in the same order, present only when one of them is not UTF-8 (`removed` then holds the lossy forms).

error.description: An error record: the structured twin of a diagnostic the tool also printed on standard error, in order with the other records.
The diagnostic as printed on standard error, without the `tool: ` prefix.

path.description: The file the diagnostic names first, as given.

path_bytes.description: The bytes of `path`, base64, present only when they are not UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form).

errno.description: The system error number, when the diagnostic ends with its message (2 for `No such file or directory`).
